entities.evidence: Yahweh is the personal name of the God who commanded Noah and then shut him in the ark. Both clauses carry the same source bearer tag, supporting reuse of the previously proposed Yahweh key.

review.translation: [And those who went in|0], [male|1] [and female|2] [from all|3] [flesh|4], [went in|5] [just as|6] [God|9] [had commanded|7] [him|8]. [Then|10] [Yahweh|11] [shut|10] [him in|12].

analysis.evidence: זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה מִכָּל בָּשָׂר identifies those entering as male and female creatures of every kind. The finite verb בָּאוּ resumes the participle and confirms their entry into the ark, which the closing clause depicts YHWH shutting behind Noah.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ plus definite article הַ plus Qal active participle, masculine plural absolute, used substantivally.

analysis.evidence: זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה means “male and female.” The pair identifies the sexes of those who entered the ark.

draft.change: Include the animal use alongside the human use under a single sense of נְקֵבָה.
draft.definition: A female, whether human or animal.
draft.evidence: Genesis 6:19 pairs נְקֵבָה with זָכָר for the animals entering the ark. Genesis 1:27 uses the same pair for humankind.

article.summary: נְקֵבָה designates a female. Genesis pairs it with זָכָר, ‘male,’ both for humankind at creation and for the animals entering the ark.

evidence.note: Two of each are to enter the ark. זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה specifies one male and one female.
God creates humankind זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה, ‘male and female.’

opposites.note: The male is the other member of the pair.

analysis.evidence: זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה, “male and female,” describes the animals entering the ark. נְקֵבָה denotes the female counterpart to זָכָר.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ־ “and” prefixed to a feminine singular absolute common noun.
analysis.sense: The female of an animal pair.

analysis.evidence: In מִכָּל בָּשָׂר (“from all flesh”), כֹּל quantifies the collective noun בָּשָׂר. The male and female entrants come from that whole group.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with prefixed מִן (“from”). The נ assimilates to the following כ, marked by the dagesh.

analysis.evidence: מִכָּל בָּשָׂר means “from among all living creatures.” זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה (“male and female”) describes the creatures that entered the ark.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, used collectively.
analysis.sense: all flesh: every living creature; mankind

analysis.evidence: בָּאוּ states what the male and female creatures did. The ark is the implied destination, and וַיִּסְגֹּר יַהְוֶה בַּעֲדוֹ describes YHWH shutting Noah in after they entered.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person common plural

analysis.evidence: כַּאֲשֶׁר links בָּאוּ (“they came”) to צִוָּה אֹתוֹ אֱלֹהִים (“God had commanded him”). The animals came in as God had commanded Noah.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed preposition כַּ־ with the indeclinable relative particle אֲשֶׁר.
analysis.sense: with a preposition: as, where, than, until

analysis.evidence: כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה אֹתוֹ אֱלֹהִים means “as God had commanded him.” God is the subject, and אֹתוֹ refers to Noah, who received the command.
analysis.morphology: Piel perfect, third person masculine singular

draft.change: Add Genesis 7:16 as evidence for the existing object-pronoun sense in et.
draft.definition: אֵת carries a pronominal suffix to express the direct object separately from the verb.
draft.evidence: Genesis 7:16 uses אֹתוֹ for the person whom God commanded.

analysis.evidence: In כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה אֹתוֹ אֱלֹהִים, “as God had commanded him,” אֱלֹהִים is the subject of צִוָּה. The suffix on אֹתוֹ refers to Noah, the person God commanded.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle in its suffixed form אֹת־ with the third-person masculine singular pronominal suffix וֹ.
analysis.sense: Marks the suffixed pronoun as the direct object of the verb.

analysis.evidence: In כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה אֹתוֹ אֱלֹהִים (“as God had commanded him”), אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the masculine singular verb צִוָּה. The plural noun form refers to the one God who commanded Noah.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute, with singular agreement.

analysis.evidence: After the animals enter the ark, יַהְוֶה is the subject of וַיִּסְגֹּר. The phrase בַּעֲדוֹ means “behind him” and refers to Noah. The ark’s entrance is the implied object.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ and no suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּסְגֹּר יַהְוֶה בַּעֲדוֹ, “Yahweh shut him in,” יַהְוֶה is the subject of the masculine singular verb וַיִּסְגֹּר. The name identifies the God who had commanded Noah in the preceding clause.
analysis.morphology: Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: After the account of entry into the ark, וַיִּסְגֹּר יַהְוֶה בַּעֲדוֹ says that YHWH shut it behind Noah, enclosing him inside.
analysis.morphology: Preposition with the third-person masculine singular pronominal suffix ־וֹ, referring to Noah.
